description: A gently curving sequence of low, linear embankments and paired moats forming a semicircular ‘half-ring’ approximately 300 m across. The feature exhibits consistent width (~10–15 m) and slight elevation (~0.5–1 m) above the surrounding terrain, with concave inner slopes suggestive of water‐retention bunds.

A faint, straight, NW–SE trending linear ridge extending roughly 800 m, with flanking shallow ditches on both sides. The alignment is rectilinear (bearing ~135°) and cuts across natural microtopography, indicative of a former causeway or canal bank.

An elongate, slightly raised platform (approx. 400 m × 150 m) with sharp corners and flat summit plateau. Subtle moat‐like depressions border three sides; the rectangular geometry strongly departs from natural hill forms.

A cluster of small, circular to sub‐circular mounds (diameter ~30–50 m) arranged along a N–S trending axis. These may represent raised‐field cells or garden plots, spaced at regular intervals (~100 m).
